trial_court: Additional Principal Judge (Family Court), Jammu - MA no.40/2023
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The parties entered into a love marriage in 1988 and had a daughter in 1990. The respondent filed for divorce under Section 13 of the J&K Hindu Marriage Act in 2012, citing cruelty. The trial court granted the relief claimed by the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: Cruelty may be mental or physical, intentional or unintentional.
legal_principles.held: It is the conduct in relation to or in respect of matrimonial duties and obligations. It is course of conduct and one which is adversely affecting the other.

legal_principles.principle: The test of cruelty is whether the conduct charged as cruelty is of such a character as to cause in the mind of the petitioner or a reasonable apprehension that it will be harmful or injurious.
legal_principles.held: Enquiry, therefore, has to be whether the conduct charged as cruelty is of such a character as to cause in the mind of the petitioner or a reasonable apprehension that it will be harmful or injurious for him to live with the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: Mental cruelty is a state of mind and feeling with one spouse due to the behavioural pattern by the other.
legal_principles.held: A feeling of anguish, disappointment and frustration in one spouse caused by the conduct of the other, can only be appreciated on assessing.

legal_principles.principle: Normal wrangling in a family life is obvious and cannot be treated as a matter of cruelty.
legal_principles.held: While arguing, the Ld. Counsel for the respondent submitted that normal wrangling in a family life is obvious and cannot be treated as a matter of cruelty.

outcome.final_order: The final order was that the judgment and decree passed by the trial court were set aside.
